evals.name: range-from-latest-tag-save-to-file
evals.prompt: 가장 최근 릴리즈 태그부터 지금까지 개발한 내용을 QA한테 넘길 문서로 정리해줘. QA는 코드 못 읽으니까 뭐가 바뀌었고 뭘 테스트해야 하는지 알 수 있어야 해. docs/handoff/ 아래에 파일로 저장해줘.
evals.expected_output: A markdown file under docs/handoff/ whose name contains no slashes or spaces, following assets/handoff-template.md: header stating the resolved range and how it was resolved, at-a-glance block, a plain-language change table where each row states the before → after the user observes and cites commit hashes, a separate internal-changes list for invisible refactors each with a reason, a QA checklist where every item has preconditions / numbered steps / expected result and a must-pass or secondary priority, a regression-watch table, a glossary, and open questions naming who to ask. The range is resolved from the tag actually reachable from HEAD (not a hardcoded version), and the resolution is stated rather than assumed.

evals.name: weekly-summary-asks-destination
evals.prompt: 이번 주에 머지된 커밋들 정리해서 기획팀이랑 QA가 같이 볼 수 있게 변경사항 요약 + 확인 체크리스트 뽑아줘
evals.expected_output: Two-part document: a one-screen summary readable by a planner (what changed, affected areas, deploy notes) followed by a QA checklist in which every item carries a must-pass or secondary priority plus preconditions, steps, and expected result. The range is derived without asking (rolling 7 days) and both the range and that interpretation are stated. Commits with no user-visible effect appear in the internal-changes list, each with a clause explaining why they are invisible, rather than as checklist items. Because the ask is to produce a document and no destination was given, the assistant asks where to put it (file / conversation / Confluence) before writing anything.

evals.name: release-eve-answers-in-conversation
evals.prompt: 내일 릴리즈인데 QA가 뭘 봐야 할지 물어봐. 최근 태그 이후 변경점 중에 사용자가 실제로 체감하는 것만 뽑아서 알려줘.
evals.expected_output: An answer in the conversation — no file written and no destination question, because the ask is a question rather than a document request — scoped to the newest reachable tag..HEAD, listing only user-observable changes with the before → after difference, plus a checklist marking which items block the release. Internal-only commits appear as a short bulleted list with a reason and commit reference, not folded into the checklist. Any change the assistant could not classify from the diff appears as an open question naming the commit author instead of a guessed expected result. If the range resolves to zero commits, it reports that instead of producing a summary.
